scope: Theorem 2.5 (A determinant criterion for all powers) of the manuscript “Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers” (preprints/Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c035db86eb706573), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let A be a complex abelian variety, H = H1(A, Q), J = Hdg(H), and R = Jder. Suppose the following data exist. (a) A rational Hodge summand H0 ⊂ H has toric Hodge group. Choose a decomposition of H0,k into CM embedding lines, with repeated occurrences distinguished, and call this finite list E0. (b) The complement of H0,k is a direct sum of blocks of nonzero admissible spaces. In a symplectic or an orthogonal block, each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to a representative Vi chosen as an actual summand of that block, with, respectively, an alternating or a symmetric pair tensor on itself. A linear block has dim Vi ≥ 2, with Vi again an actual summand, and each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to either Vi or V i, paired with each other as in Lemma 2.2. The pair identifies V i with V ∗ i (−1) as a Hodge-graded space and with the dual as a group representation. (c) Under these identifications the image of Rk contains P = Y i∈ISp Sp(Vi) × Y i∈ISO SO(Vi) × Y i∈ISL SL(Vi). Each factor acts by its standard representation on its own copies, by the dual representation on the opposite copies of a linear block, and trivially on every other block and on H0,k. The symplectic and orthogonal forms are the inverse pairings. (d) Let W1, . . . , Ws be any list, with arbitrary repetitions, from {Vi : i ∈ ISO} ∪ {Vi, V i : i ∈ ISL}. Whenever there are ℓ1, . . . , ℓr ∈ E0, again with arbitrary repetitions, such that s X j=1 ϵγ(Wj) + r X a=1 ϵγ(ℓa) = 0 for every γ ∈ Gal(k/Q), (2.3) the line Ns j=1 D(Wj) is CM-supplied on its separate tensor slots. Empty lists are allowed. Then for every p ≥ 0 every rational balanced tensor in H⊗2p is the class of a rational algebraic cycle on its separate A-slots. The rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension of Am for every m ≥ 1. Call the data saturated if every singleton D(Vi) for an orthogonal or linear block is CM-supplied, without any balance condition. For saturated data and any CM abelian variety M, the induced data on A × M are saturated. In particular the same tensor and Hodge-conjecture conclusions hold for every power of A × M.
